newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan Central Bank CD auction yields fall.
newsitem.headline: Jordan Central Bank CD auction yields fall.

text.p: The Central Bank of Jordan on Thursday said yields dropped in its latest 100 million dinars ($141 million) bi-monthly CD auction, the second time since it introduced a market-dictated auction system last month.

The average yield on the second competitive bi-monthly certificate of deposit (CDs) auction which closed on Thursday fell on three-month paper to 8.52 percent from 8.825 percent at the last auction. Six-month paper also dropped to 8.75 percent from 9.033 percent in the last auction.
The yield offers accepted varied on three-month paper from a 8.70 percent high to a 8.50 percent low compared to the range of 8.90 percent high to 8.750 percent low in the last auction.
Six-month CDs yield offers accepted ranged from a high of 8.8125 percent to 8.625 percent low against a range from a 9.10 percent high to 9.000 percent low.
Total bids received were 197 million dinars of which 70.5 million dinars were for three-month paper and the remaining 126.5 million dinars bids offered for six-month paper.
The three-month paper was covered 1.42 times while the six-month paper was covered 2.53 times.
The Central Bank sold 50 million dinars worth of three-month CDs and 50 million dinars of six month CDs.

The Central Bank introduced last month for the first time a market-dictated CD auction system and began announcing yields in line with supply and demand as part of moves to adopt a move flexible interest rates structure.
Previously interest rates on three-month paper had been fixed for over a year at 9.25 percent and for six-month paper at 9.50 percent.
The Central Bank keeps a high interest rate policy to make dinar-denominated assets attractive and prevent a flow of dinars into dollar-denominated assets.
